correctness.rationale: Barycentric membership is equivalent to the top s=r+1 coordinate sum f_s(p)≥α=1/(1+λ): the support mass criterion gives a sparse face vector and residual simplex vector in both directions. In the barycentric subdivision, f_s is affine on each order chamber; vertices indexed by subsets I have f_s(b_I)=min(1,s/|I|). Removing low-valued vertices by normalized positive barycentric weights gives a coherent facewise strong deformation retract to skel_{k−1} for k=floor[s(1+λ)]≤d; equalities include new subcomplex at each threshold. Standard simplex-skeleton cellular homology yields wedge of C(d,k) spheres S^(k−1), and compatible inclusions imply stated integral bars. min f_s=s/n only at centroid gives exact λ*=(n−s)/s. The last-phase void is a translated ε-scaled sum-zero polar hypersimplex; braid-chamber vertices b_j/q_j with q_j=min(s,j)−sj/n, Gram determinant 1/n and n! chambers give C_{d,r}. The extremal lower coordinate ensures no simplex clipping for λ≥(d−s)/s. Independently checked C formula against ∏q_j for all s in dimensions d=2..6; finite checks supplement all-d proof.
